provider: WFG National Title Insurance Company — Seller Net Sheet Rate Calculator (rates.wfgnationaltitle.com)
scenario: $500,000 purchase price, $400,000 loan amount, Hinds County (MS's most-populous/standard-scenario county), residential resale (SettlementStatementVersion: CD).
methodology: Solved this session by extracting the calculator's own Angular "sellerNetForm" component logic from its lazy-loaded route chunk (webpack chunk 7, hash 8a01902021d264bdb338 -- fetched by replaying the runtime bundle's own chunk-hash map, since this route is not referenced in the shell page's main.js until a user actually clicks into the seller-net-sheet flow). This resolved the 2026-08-07 session's blocker: `POST /api/rates/fees/estimatefeesforsellernet` was 500ing with unhelpful ProblemDetails errors because the guessed flat `PropertyState`/`PropertyCounty`/`PropertyCity` fields (borrowed from the sibling, differently-shaped `sellernet/calculate` endpoint's own validation-error field names) do not match this endpoint's real schema. The component's own `prepareCalculateFeeRequest()` method reveals the actual required body: `Properties: [{City, County, IsPrimary: true, State}]` (nested, not flat), `Loans: [{LienPosition: 0, LoanAmount}]`, `TransactionProductType: {ProductTypeId: 0, TransactionTypeId: 0}` (0/0 confirmed correct for this flow, not a placeholder), `calculateTaxRequest: {}` (an empty class instance), `SettlementStatementVersion: "CD"`, and empty arrays/objects for `premiumDiscounts`/`Endorsements`/`PriorLenderPolicy`/`PriorOwnerPolicy`. Driven via a plain Content-Type: application/json HTTP POST, no browser/JS execution needed. Confirmed via `GET /api/rates/State/GetCalculationEnabledStates` (also public, no auth) that this one API has `isCalculationEnabled: true` for 47 states + DC -- a single new, genuinely distinct 5th major-underwriter source (WFG National Title, a separate corporate family from FNF/Old Republic/Stewart/First American, all already on file elsewhere in this survey) usable across nearly every remaining below-threshold scarce state in one technique. No personal-data field (name/email/phone) exists anywhere in this request shape. Separately confirmed via static inspection of the same chunk's hardcoded `feesConfiguration` sort-weight table that WFG has only itemized its settlement/closing HUD-fee line items for 7 states (WA, CA, TX, OR, AZ, NV, CO) -- for every other state (including this one) the tool returns a premium-only result (Owner's Title Insurance Premium, no settlement/search/doc-prep breakdown), which per this project's 2026-08-05 FNF scoping correction is still valid, dated calculator-harvest evidence.

provider: Old Republic Title Insurance Company — Rate Calculator (ortratecalculator.oldrepublictitle.com)
scenario: $500,000 purchase price (OWNERS category) and $400,000 loan amount (LOAN category), statewide, computed as two separate standalone quotes -- see methodology.
methodology: This is Old Republic's *second* calculator tool (distinct from `ortconline.com/Web2`, whose own footprint does not include MS -- see CALCULATORS.md's state-coverage note). This state was not previously known to be NoBot-blocked or otherwise tried on this tool; harvested for the first time this session as part of the same NoBot-loosening follow-up that unlocked SC/LA (see those states' parallel entries). MS's `RadPolicyCategory` radio group offers only 4 categories (OWNERS, LOAN, HOME EQUITY, MISCELLANEOUS) -- unlike SC's dedicated "SIMULTANEOUS LOAN & OWNERS" option or LA's combined "PURCHASE/SALE" category, MS has no simultaneous-issue category, so Owner's and Lender's premiums had to be queried as two separate single-category calculations rather than one combined quote: (1) OWNERS category (default-checked), POST `txtLiabilityAmt=500000` (own __EVENTTARGET) then `btnCalculate=Calculate`; (2) fresh POST selecting `RadPolicyCategory=2` (LOAN, own __EVENTTARGET, which swaps the visible liability field from `txtLiabilityAmt` to `txtCrLiabilityAmt`), POST `txtCrLiabilityAmt=400000` (own __EVENTTARGET) then `btnCalculate=Calculate`. **Gotcha**: posting `txtCrLiabilityAmt` while the OWNERS category is still selected (i.e. without first switching to LOAN) throws a hard HTTP 500 (`ErrorPage500.aspx`) -- the field genuinely does not exist in that category's rendered DOM, the same 'posting a field not in the DOM breaks the postback' failure mode already documented elsewhere in this project (Old Republic's `ortconline.com` ReoList/OR-county gotchas). No county selector was required or offered by this tool for MS (statewide pricing). No personal-data fields anywhere in this flow.
